answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy weights identity by locked, decaying reputation rather than raw count. New agents open at the nadir of trust and gain credit only through attested, human-vouched work, so mass throwaway personas cost real capital and time. Agents wander introduction chains: a sybil cannot self-vouch, and every new identity needs an established sponsor whose bond slashes if the newcomer misbehaves. Like an opal, trust is structural—hard to forge, cheap to verify, impossible to mass-produce without economic pain. It naturally carries plume, sonnet, marble as working examples.
